boundary_updates.evidence: Step 1.2 separately treats v^0=0 by h(s)=t0+s-s0, with h''=0, and v^0 nonzero by the explicit logarithmic local reparametrization. Step 1.3 separates y=x-dot^0 identically zero from its nowhere-zero branch before dividing by y.

Step 1.2 fixes an interior t0 of the open source interval and s0, shrinks an open J so 1+2v^0(s-s0)>0 and h(J) lies in the source interval, and has h(s0)=t0. The claim is local at every parameter value; no endpoint extension or global reparametrization is asserted. Step 1.3 proves the converse locally.

Step 1.2 uses a supplied t0,s0 and a sufficiently small single open interval J; step 1.3 obtains c^a as constant ratios on the nowhere-zero branch. These are finite local constructions, with no selection over a family of paths beyond the inherited ambient countable-choice convention.

When X0=W0=0, the explicit comparison solution in step 1.2 is identically zero and R0=0. Step 1.3 uses R'=max(1/2,R0), so K'=closed B_{R'} remains a positive-radius compact convex subset of U_L containing both paths under H1. No division by initial amplitude or velocity occurs; epsilon stays positive as required.

Step 1.2 solves the comparison system on the entire closed interval [0,S_*]; step 1.3 bounds its range and, under H1, the scaled geodesic range there. Step 2.1 applies the supplier supremum estimate over [0,S_*], including S=0 and S=S_*.

The Statement assumes r>0 and z nonzero everywhere. In step 4.1, E(r)=q_TT=-z, so E(r) is nonzero on the whole shrunken coordinate rectangle and F/E is smooth. Only after removing the cross term is q_rr=1/z inferred. Points with r=s, where z=0, are excluded; the Remarks explicitly allow r to vary across that excluded level in a larger horizon-crossing chart.

Step 4.1 defines the null radial scalar at t=0, with phi(0)=0 and phi(hat s)=1, and proves its continuous endpoint extension. Step 2.3 treats the final-null case t1=1 separately from t1<1 and passes to the initial boundary t1 by continuity and integrability. Step 5.2 gives phi(0)=0 and phi(1)=1 for the maximizing radial representation.

Under clause (d)'s additional nonvanishing hypotheses, step 5.2 derives sigma'=lambda P almost everywhere from length equality, applies the direction argument of step 4.1, rules out t1>0, and constructs the absolutely continuous nondecreasing surjection phi:[0,1] to [0,1].

The converse part of step 5.2 computes the length of an absolutely continuous nondecreasing surjective reparametrization of the radial geodesic as sqrt(-g_p(v0,v0)), proving equality. Step 6.1 separately proves radial future-causal/timelike vectors give the corresponding reachable endpoints.

For Omega empty, the existential definitions of J^+(Omega) and I^+(Omega) both give empty sets, so all identities of clause (d) are empty-set equalities. Step 6.1 proves the inclusions by witnesses x in Omega; with no such witness their forward implications are vacuous, and their reverse reflexive-witness implications are likewise vacuous.

For Omega={x}, step 6.1 uses precisely that x as its source witness. The reverse inclusions use the reflexive relation x<=x (or the endpoint witness for J^+(I^+(Omega))); no distinct second member of Omega is needed. The pointwise implications used are steps 3.1 and 4.1.

Step 6.1 proves I^+(J^+(Omega)) subset I^+(Omega) from x<=y and y<<z using clause (b), proved in step 4.1; it proves J^+(I^+(Omega)) subset I^+(Omega) from x<<y and y<=z using clause (a), proved in step 3.1. Time reversal gives the past identities.

In step 6.1, reflexivity supplies the reverse inclusion I^+(Omega) subset I^+(J^+(Omega)); for J^+(I^+(Omega)), take the chronologically reached endpoint itself as the intermediate point and its reflexive causal successor. The same witnesses work after time reversal.

Step 1.1 sets tau_q=0 outside J^-(q) and at q and states positivity exactly on I^-(q). Step 3.2 handles limsup tau_q(r_n)=0 before selecting curves; in the positive-limsup branch it rules out b=0 using L_g(alpha_n)<=C b_n, so the bounded positive-domain limit theorem is applied only with b>0.

Step 2.1 treats distinct endpoints r!=q with b>=d_h(r,q)>0 and normalizes the actual approximating curves onto the common closed domain [0,1]. Step 3.1 gives the radial formula and its zero extension at q/outside causal past. Step 3.2 keeps variable initial endpoints in a compact set and again normalizes curves on [0,1].

Step 2.1 uses Countable Choice for length-approximating curves only for r in J^-(q) minus {q}, a nonempty curve class. Step 3.2 selects approximating curves only after discarding zero-separation terms in a positive-limsup subsequence. Completeness and limit suppliers retain their declared DC/CC hypotheses; no arbitrary-index choice is introduced.

Definition (a) fixes inertia (3,1,0) on each tangent fibre: there is exactly one negative direction and three positive directions in a diagonalizing basis. That one negative direction is included in the ordinary four-dimensional metric; a one-dimensional manifold is outside the opening four-manifold hypothesis.

The opening data are one affine connection on a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. Clauses (a)-(c) define its compatibility/torsion tests and the class LC(M,g); they impose no one-dimensional specialization and do not themselves assert that this connection class has one member. Existence/uniqueness is supplied separately.

At a supplied p in the matter domain, Definition tests an individual vector v but each condition quantifies over every vector of the specified causal type in the four-dimensional tangent space. Testing one vector alone is not asserted to suffice; the single-point definition introduces no one-dimensional or singleton-family reduction.
